title: Block Is Back
snippet: Last week, CashApp launched CashApp Tags, a $25 line of Near Field Communication (NFC)-enabled charms that connect to your CashApp Card and let you tap and pay with accessories like a magic wand.
content_html:
By: Varshika Prasanna, Research Analyst, Fintech

Last week, CashApp launched CashApp Tags, a $25 line of Near Field Communication (NFC)-enabled charms that connect to your CashApp Card and let you tap and pay with accessories like a magic wand.

Inspired by the viral “pay with magic” videos, where people jokingly stuffed payment cards into toy wands, Block turned an internet joke into a real product. The first drop sold out fast, with more form factors and colors slated through the summer.

While CashApp Tags seem whimsical, they reveal how Block is making consumer finance fun again.

As visible, shareable accessories, CashApp Tags generate organic awareness and engagement in a way traditional payment products rarely do. The product is well suited to younger users, with ~1 in 5 American teens already carrying a CashApp Card, adding personality and self-expression to everyday spending. For adults, the appeal is novelty, a conversation piece that drives word of mouth discovery. In an increasingly crowded fintech landscape, products that spark attention can become powerful, low-cost customer acquisition channels.

Importantly, the launch feels uniquely Block. The marketing is quirky, playful, and culturally fluent, an echo of CashApp’s earlier identity, when the brand built affinity through grassroots campus adoption, social sharing, and a strong presence in internet culture. As peer-to-peer payments commoditize, CashApp Tags make transactions more expressive and could help CashApp drive incremental monthly active user (MAU) growth.

The launch also highlights something investors have waited to see. Product velocity is returning to Block.

Hardware is notoriously difficult to execute, requiring coordination across design, manufacturing, software, and distribution. But Block has deep hardware roots dating to its origins as Square, whose first card reader turned smartphones into point-of-sale terminals. CashApp Tags extend that expertise into the consumer ecosystem and reveal the benefits of Block’s earlier organizational restructuring.

Over the past few years, Block has fundamentally reshaped how it operates. The company moved away from siloed business units toward functional teams while reducing headcount by roughly 40%. Engineering, design, and hardware now operate as shared capabilities rather than isolated product organizations. Now, ideas at Block can move more quickly from concept to launch regardless of whether they originate in Square, Cash App, or elsewhere.

The result is a more integrated company shipping product faster than ever.

And that focus is already showing up in the numbers. In the first quarter, Cash App gross profit growth accelerated to 38% year over year while Square gross profit growth accelerated to 9%. Management also raised full-year guidance, signaling strength across both ecosystems.

AI is central to the acceleration.

Goose, Block’s internal automation layer, is accessed by employees through BuilderBot, an AI development interface that lets anyone inside the company build or modify product features straight from Slack. Between January and April 2026, management noted that code changes per engineer rose more than 2.5x, a direct read on rising productivity.

Block is embedding AI directly into its external ecosystems too. On the seller side, ManagerBot functions as an AI co-founder, helping merchants analyze performance, identify opportunities, and operate more efficiently. ManagerBot is currently live in open beta across more than 1 million sellers. On the consumer side, MoneyBot serves as a financial assistant, helping users manage spending, discover offers, and take action within Cash App. MoneyBot continues to scale throughout the Cash App ecosystem ahead of a broader launch expected later this month.

Both products are evolving beyond simple chat interfaces into proactive intelligence layers. Instead of waiting for users to ask questions, they increasingly surface recommendations and actions on their own. Management noted that roughly 70% of conversations now begin with proactive prompts.

The retention data is what stands out. Sellers who complete an insight session with ManagerBot are 33% more likely to return to Block. Cash App users are five times more likely to revisit MoneyBot after taking a recommended action. In our view, these early signals suggest AI can strengthen engagement and retention on both sides of Block’s network.

That matters because it sets the stage for what we believe is Block’s most important long-term opportunity.

Neighborhoods.

Neighborhoods connects Cash App’s 59 million consumer base with millions of Square sellers. Merchants can attract local customers, build followers, promote products, and offer rewards. Consumers can discover businesses, redeem offers, and transact seamlessly within Cash App. Early signals are promising, with adoption accelerating and ~100,000 Cash App users already following local sellers, according to management.

The economics are compelling. By keeping transactions within its own two-sided network, Block can process Neighborhoods payments at a ~1% fee, less than half the ~2.5% typically charged through traditional card networks. Combined with loyalty programs that reward repeat spending, Neighborhoods has the potential to create a local commerce network within block and deepen engagement on both sides of the network, driving monthly active user growth at Cash App and payment volume growth among Square sellers while strengthening Block’s two-sided ecosystem.

Neighborhoods has long been central to our Block thesis. The idea was always straightforward: unlock the network effects of owning a two-sided ecosystem to drive local commerce. For years, that vision was more promise than reality.

What has changed is execution.

A faster, flatter, and more focused Block is finally shipping the products required to connect both sides of the ecosystem. The wheels are now set in motion for Neighborhoods to play out.

Block is back.
